mainTopic: Checking the וושט for a possible clawing, עולא's thorn ruling, the תורבץ הוושט, and רבא's bull ruling that combined רב's and שמואל's stringencies
overview: This amud opens by explaining why רבה said the וושט may be checked only from the inside: it matters for ספק דרוסה, because the redness of a clawing shows only on the white inside. In a story, רבה checks from the outside and אביי reminds him of his own rule. רבה then finds two drops of blood inside and rules the animal a טריפה; he was only testing אביי. Next עולא rules that a thorn stuck in the וושט does not make us worry about a hole that healed. The גמרא defends this against four comparisons, and רב כהנא explains that the ruling covers even a thorn embedded in the wall. Then רב and שמואל argue about a hole in the תורבץ הוושט, and the גמרא tries to define exactly where that area is. רבא rules a bull טריפה by combining the strict sides of רב and שמואל. רבי אבא overturns this and makes רבא pay the owner. The amud ends as מר בריה דרבינא starts a ברייתא against mixing opinions, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The inside-only check is needed for a possible clawing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers why רבה said the וושט may be checked only from the inside: his rule is about ספק דרוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule is needed for a case where we are unsure if the animal was clawed by a predator.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question asked just before this section: why must the וושט be checked only from the inside? The answer is that the rule is about a case where we are unsure if the animal was clawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a simple hole, you could look from either side. A דרוסה shows up as redness, and the outside of the וושט is red anyway. Only the white inside can show whether the clawing left its mark.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt; we are not sure
An animal clawed by a predator, which makes it a טריפה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the inside-only check is not a rule for every kind of damage. It applies to checking for a דרוסה, which can only be seen on the white inside.

phrases.english: For a case of uncertain clawing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous section about רבה's inside-only rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the rule applies to ספק דרוסה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Why not check from the outside too, if a hole could be seen from either side?
steps.terutzMaskana: For a possible clawing, the redness can only be seen on the white inside, so the inside must be checked.

steps.title: רבה checks a possibly clawed animal from the outside
steps.stepSummary: A ספק דרוסה case comes to רבה, and he starts checking the וושט from the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain animal that might have been clawed came before רבה. רבה was checking its gullet from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case. This sets up the next move, because רבה seems to be going against his own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous step we learned that a ספק דרוסה must be checked from the inside. Here רבה, who made that rule, checks from the outside. This sets up a surprise.

phrases.english: A certain case of uncertain clawing
that came before Rabba,
Rabba was checking it
the gullet, from the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא סְפֵק דְּרוּסָה דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story about the exact case from Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבה is checking a ספק דרוסה from the outside.

steps.title: אביי reminds רבה of his own rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: you yourself said the וושט may only be checked from the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But aren't you, master, the one who said the gullet may only be checked from the inside?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, the student, points out that his teacher רבה is doing the opposite of what רבה himself taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge uses רבה's own words against his action. If the inside-only rule is about ספק דרוסה, then checking this case from the outside does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it you, master, who said...

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But isn't it you, master, who said:
The gullet has no checking
except from the inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's action in Step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's checking of the וושט from the outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contradiction between רבה's own ruling (check only from the inside) and what he is doing.

steps.title: רבה checks the inside, finds blood, and rules it a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבה turns the וושט inside out, finds two drops of blood, and declares the animal a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה turned it over and checked it. He found two drops of blood on it, and he declared it a טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה accepts אביי's reminder. He checks the inside and finds signs of clawing, so the animal is not kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves the rule from Step 1 in real life. The blood could not be seen from the red outside. Once the white inside was checked, the clawing showed up, and the animal became a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: He declared it a טריפה (not kosher)

steps.whatToRemember: A ספק דרוסה on the וושט is checked on the inside, where even two drops of blood can show the clawing.

phrases.english: Rabba turned it over and checked it,
and two drops of blood were found on it,
and he declared it a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה responds to אביי's challenge by doing it correctly
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Checking from the inside revealed the clawing, so the animal was ruled a טריפה.

steps.title: רבה was only testing אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבה did not forget his rule. He wanted to sharpen אביי's mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה, too, only wanted to sharpen אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: how could רבה forget his own rule? He didn't forget. He was testing his student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this line we might think רבה made a mistake about his own teaching. The גמרא tells us he checked from the outside on purpose, to see whether אביי would notice and speak up.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה changed his mind or made a mistake. His rule stays the same. He checked from the outside only as a test.

phrases.english: And Rabba too
wanted only to sharpen Abaye.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה נָמֵי לְחַדּוֹדֵי לְאַבָּיֵי הוּא דְּבָעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבה's strange behavior in Step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the intent behind an action
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה remembered his rule. He acted this way only to test and sharpen אביי.

steps.title: עולא: a thorn stuck in the gullet is not suspected of a healed hole
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that if a thorn is found stuck in the וושט, we do not suspect it pierced through earlier and the hole healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: If a thorn is stuck in the gullet, we do not worry that perhaps it pierced through and then healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from עולא about a thorn found stuck in the וושט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thorn stuck in the וושט might have pierced all the way through, and a hole there makes the animal a טריפה. Someone might worry that it pierced and then healed over, so the hole is hidden. עולא says we do not have that worry, and the animal stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: We are not concerned; we don't worry

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the subject of several challenges that follow, listed in the סימן.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
If a thorn sat in the gullet,
phrases.notes: "Sat" means it was found stuck there.

phrases.english: we are not concerned that perhaps it healed.
phrases.notes: The worry would be that it made a hole that then closed up. עולא says we don't think that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: יָשַׁב לוֹ קוֹץ בַּוֶּושֶׁט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about the וושט
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thorn stuck in the וושט does not make us suspect a hole that healed over; the animal is kosher.

steps.title: A memory list for the coming challenges to עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a memory list of key words for the questions about עולא's ruling that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Clawed, pieces, with a knife, impure. This is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is listing key words so we can remember the order of the challenges against עולא that are about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one upcoming question. דרס hints at a clawing case, חתיכות at a case of pieces, בסכין at a case with a knife, and טמאה at a case of impurity. The list itself rules nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid listing what comes next

phrases.english: (Clawed, pieces,
phrases.notes: Here the round brackets just set off a memory list. Each word hints at a question coming up next.

phrases.english: with a knife, impure: a mnemonic)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prepares the challenges against עולא's ruling in Step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a memory list for the coming challenges.

steps.title: Why is this different from a doubt about clawing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how עולא can be lenient when, in a case of ספק דרוסה, we are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to עולא, how is this different from a doubt about whether the animal was clawed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens the first of four challenges to עולא. It points to ספק דרוסה, a doubt where the animal is not simply assumed to be kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the thorn case there is a doubt, and עולא is lenient. In a case of ספק דרוסה we do not simply assume the animal is fine. So why should the thorn case be any different?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? A formula for comparing two cases that seem alike.
A doubt about whether a predator clawed the animal, which would make it a טריפה.

phrases.english: But according to Ulla, how is this different from a doubt about clawing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the questions on עולא's ruling that the memory list in step 7 pointed to.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's lenient ruling about the thorn in the וושט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A similar doubt about clawing is treated strictly, so the thorn case should be strict too.

steps.title: עולא is not concerned about a doubt of clawing either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עולא holds we are not concerned with ספק דרוסה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא holds that we are not concerned about a doubt of clawing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first challenge. עולא simply does not accept that ספק דרוסה is treated strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed everyone is strict about ספק דרוסה. The answer says עולא disagrees with that assumption. So for him there is no contradiction: he is lenient in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; he is of the opinion.
We are not concerned; we do not worry about this possibility.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר עוּלָּא אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לִסְפֵק דְּרוּסָה.
phrases.english: Ulla holds that we are not concerned about a doubt of clawing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the premise: עולא is not strict about ספק דרוסה either.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought ספק דרוסה is always treated strictly, which would clash with עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא is consistent: he is lenient about ספק דרוסה and about the thorn.

steps.title: Why is this different from two pieces of fat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares the thorn case to two pieces of fat, one forbidden חלב and one permitted שומן, where a doubt is treated strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from two pieces, one of forbidden fat and one of permitted fat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge. When someone has two pieces, one חלב and one שומן, and does not know which he ate, we are strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too there is a doubt, yet we do not assume he ate the permitted piece. So why should we assume the best in the thorn case?

phrases.english: And how is this different from two pieces,
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes the familiar case: a person ate one of the two pieces and does not know which one.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חֵלֶב וְאַחַת שֶׁל שׁוּמָּן?
phrases.english: one of forbidden fat and one of permitted fat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second comparison case against עולא, after the first was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's lenient ruling about the thorn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the two-pieces case a doubt is treated strictly, so the thorn doubt should be strict too.

steps.title: There, a prohibition was already established
steps.stepSummary: In the two-pieces case, one piece is definitely forbidden, so there is an established prohibition. The thorn case has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, a prohibition was already established.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. With the two pieces, we know for sure that something forbidden is in front of us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the fat case, the doubt starts from a known prohibition, since one piece is certainly חלב. In the thorn case there is no known prohibition to begin with, so we may be lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition was established; we know for sure that something forbidden is present.

phrases.english: There, a prohibition was established.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: one has an established prohibition, the other does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every doubt about something forbidden should be treated strictly.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strictness applies when a prohibition is known to be present; the thorn case has no such known prohibition.

steps.title: Why is this different from a knife found notched?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares the thorn case to someone who slaughtered and then found his knife notched, where we are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from someone who slaughters with a knife and it is found notched?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge. If a knife is found notched after slaughtering, we worry that the notch was there during the slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perhaps the knife was damaged only after the slaughter, yet the animal is forbidden. That is a doubt treated strictly, so why is the thorn case lenient?

keyTerms.meaning: Notched; having a nick in the blade, which makes the שחיטה invalid.
One who slaughters an animal according to halacha.

phrases.english: And how is this different from one who slaughters with a knife,
and it was found notched?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third comparison case against עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's lenient ruling about the thorn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With the notched knife we worry the damage came earlier, so we should worry the same way about the thorn.

steps.title: There, a flaw appeared in the knife
steps.stepSummary: In the knife case, an actual flaw was born in the knife, so we worry it was there during the slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, a flaw appeared in the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third challenge. In the knife case, there is a real flaw right in front of us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the knife clearly has a defect now, we suspect that it already had it during the שחיטה. In the thorn case, the gullet wall is whole right now, with no flaw in front of us, so we may assume it was whole before too.

phrases.english: There, a flaw was born in the knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: the knife has a proven flaw.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any doubt about whether damage came before or after the שחיטה should be strict.
steps.terutzMaskana: We are strict with the knife because a real flaw appeared in it. That reason does not apply to the thorn case.

steps.title: Why is this different from doubtful impurity in a private place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares the thorn case to ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד, which is ruled impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from a doubt about impurity in a private domain, where the doubt is ruled impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth challenge. A doubt about טומאה in a רשות היחיד is treated strictly, as impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another well-known case where a doubt leads to a strict ruling. So the question is why עולא does not treat the thorn doubt strictly in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about whether something or someone became ritually impure.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִסְּפֵק טוּמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד,
phrases.english: And how is this different from a doubt about impurity in a private domain,
where its doubt is impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִסְּפֵק טוּמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth comparison case against עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's lenient ruling about the thorn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A doubt of טומאה in a private domain is strict, so the thorn doubt should be strict too.

steps.title: The impurity rules come from סוטה and cannot be compared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that you could just as easily compare to a public domain, where a doubt is pure. The real point is that both rules are a tradition learned from סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your logic, let us compare it to a doubt about impurity in a public domain, where the doubt is pure! Rather, there, they learned the הלכה through tradition from סוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the fourth challenge in two moves. First it shows that the comparison works both ways, and then it explains that the impurity rules are a special tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we compare the thorn to טומאה, why choose רשות היחיד (strict) rather than רשות הרבים (lenient)? This shows that the טומאה rules do not follow simple logic. They are a special הלכה learned from סוטה, so we cannot use them to decide other cases like the thorn.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning; turning the questioner's logic back on him.
They learned this halacha by tradition; it is a special rule, not built from simple logic.
A woman suspected by her husband of being unfaithful.

steps.whatToRemember: All four challenges are answered, and עולא's leniency about the thorn stands. ספק דרוסה: עולא is not concerned. Two pieces of fat: there a prohibition was established. Notched knife: a real flaw appeared. ספק טומאה: it is a special tradition from סוטה.
steps.confusionAlert: The word ולטעמיך does not start a new challenge against עולא. It is the first part of the answer, showing that the questioner's comparison could just as easily point the other way.

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning, let us compare it
to a doubt about impurity in a public domain,
where its doubt is pure!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָתָם, הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ מִסּוֹטָה.
phrases.english: Rather, there, they learned this halacha by tradition from the sota.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 and closes the series of challenges to עולא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the comparison cuts both ways, then limits the impurity rules to a special tradition from סוטה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The strict rule for ספק טומאה in a private domain could teach us how to handle other doubts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rules of ספק טומאה come from a tradition learned from סוטה and cannot be applied to the thorn case.

steps.title: A scholar's version: עולא was lenient only when the thorn was found loose
steps.stepSummary: A scholar reports that עולא's leniency applied only to a thorn found loose in the gullet. If it was stuck in the wall, we worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain scholar sat before רב כהנא and said: The ruling was stated about a thorn that was 'found' in the gullet. But if it was 'sitting', stuck in the wall, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: A student offers his version of עולא's ruling about a thorn in the gullet. In his version, the ruling is narrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He limits עולא's leniency to a thorn lying loose. If the thorn was embedded in the wall, he says we must worry it pierced the gullet and the hole later healed. That would make the animal a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Was found, meaning the thorn was lying loose in the gullet
Sat, meaning the thorn was stuck into the gullet wall
We are concerned, so we treat the possible problem as real

phrases.english: One of the Sages was sitting
before רב כהנא,
and he was sitting and saying:
'Was found' is what was stated,
phrases.notes: He is quoting עולא's ruling from the earlier steps: no worry about a thorn found in the gullet.

phrases.english: but if it sat embedded, we are concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges to עולא's leniency are answered, this step asks how far that leniency reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency covers only a thorn found loose. An embedded thorn raises concern.

steps.title: רב כהנא rejects that version: the leniency covers even an embedded thorn
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says the ruling was stated about an embedded thorn. A loose thorn needed no ruling, since wild animals eat thorns all the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to them: Don't listen to him. The ruling was stated about a thorn that 'sat', stuck in the wall. A thorn simply found loose did not need עולא to rule on it, because all animals that graze outside eat thorns.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא tells everyone to ignore the scholar's version. He gives the correct one: עולא was lenient even about a thorn stuck in the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is that a loose thorn is too obvious to need a ruling. Animals in the field swallow thorns constantly, so finding one proves nothing. עולא's ruling must have been about the harder case, a thorn stuck in the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not necessary to say, because it is obvious
Animals that live outside, out in the fields

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב כהנא, עולא is lenient even when the thorn is embedded in the gullet wall.

phrases.english: רב כהנא said to them:
Do not listen to him,
'Sat' is what was stated,
but where it was simply found,
עולא did not need to say it,
since all animals that live outside
eat thorns.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב כָּהֲנָא: לָא תְּצִיתוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the narrow version given in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The scholar's claim that עולא was lenient only about a loose thorn.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A loose thorn is too obvious to need a ruling, since animals eat thorns regularly. The ruling must have been about an embedded thorn.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about a hole in the entrance of the gullet
steps.stepSummary: רב says any hole in the תורבץ הוושט makes the animal טריפה, because it counts as a place of slaughter. שמואל says only a hole through most of it does, because it is not a place of slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If the entrance of the gullet was pierced, רב says any small hole makes the animal טריפה, and שמואל says only a hole through most of it does. רב says any hole because it is a place fit for slaughter. שמואל says most of it because it is not a place fit for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב and שמואל argue about a hole in the entrance of the gullet, and each gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their argument turns on whether the תורבץ counts as part of the gullet itself. רב says yes, since you may slaughter there, so the gullet's rule applies and any hole makes it טריפה. שמואל says no, since it is not a place of slaughter, so it is treated more like the throat and only a hole through most of it counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance of the gullet, where it meets the throat
With any amount, even a tiny hole
A place on the neck where kosher slaughter is valid

steps.confusionAlert: Here רב is the strict one about holes. But calling the תורבץ a 'place of slaughter' is also what makes slaughtering there valid, and that is lenient. Each opinion has a strict side and a lenient side, and step 24 depends on this.

phrases.english: It was stated: the entrance of the gullet,
רב says: with any amount,
and שמואל says: with its majority.
רב says any amount:
it is a place of slaughter,
and שמואל says its majority:
it is not a place of slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the משנה's rule about a pierced gullet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: any hole in the תורבץ makes the animal טריפה, since it is a place of slaughter. שמואל: only a hole through most of it does, since it is not a place of slaughter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument sets up the definitions that follow and the ruling about the bull in step 24.

steps.title: Where exactly is the entrance of the gullet?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which area counts as the תורבץ הוושט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which area is the entrance of the gullet?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact location of the תורבץ. This sets up the definitions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument between רב and שמואל only matters in practice if we know where the תורבץ ends and the gullet itself begins.

phrases.english: Which is the entrance of the gullet?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the physical definition of the term argued about in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical borders of the תורבץ הוושט.

steps.title: First definition: the תורבץ widens when cut, the gullet stays in place
steps.stepSummary: Quoting שמואל, מרי בר מר עוקבא says the area that widens when cut is the תורבץ, and the area that stays in place is the gullet itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרי בר מר עוקבא said in the name of שמואל: Any area that widens when you cut it is the entrance of the gullet. Any area that stays in place when you cut it is the gullet itself.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer to the question: you tell the two areas apart by how the flesh reacts when it is cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is a physical one. Flesh that spreads open when cut is the תורבץ. Flesh that holds its position is the real gullet.

phrases.english: מרי בר מר עוקבא said
that שמואל said:
Whatever widens when cut,
this is the entrance of the gullet;
what stays in place when cut,
this is the gullet itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָרִי בַּר מָר עוּקְבָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If it widens when cut, it is the תורבץ. If it stays in place when cut, it is the gullet itself.

steps.title: רב פפי's correction: the תורבץ stays in place, the gullet contracts
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי reports that his teacher, רב ביבי בר אביי, said it differently: the area that stays in place is the תורבץ, and the gullet itself is what contracts when cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said to them: The Master did not say it that way. Who is the Master? רב ביבי בר אביי. Rather, he said: Whatever stays in place when cut is the entrance of the gullet. So which is the gullet itself? Whatever shrinks inward when cut.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי rejects the first definition and gives his teacher's version instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He moves each label one step down. The flesh that 'stays in place', which step 20 called the gullet, is really the תורבץ. The true gullet is the part that pulls inward when cut. The result is that the gullet itself begins lower than step 20 said.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master did not say it this way

phrases.english: רב פפי said to them:
The Master did not say so,
and who is he? רב ביבי בר אביי.
Rather, whatever stays in place when cut,
this is the entrance of the gullet.
Then which is the gullet itself?
Whatever constricts when cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב פַּפֵּי: מָר לָא אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the definition given in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the flesh which stays in place when cut is the gullet itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רב ביבי בר אביי, that area is the תורבץ. The real gullet is the part that contracts.

steps.title: Another view: the תורבץ is just the throat right at the gullet
steps.stepSummary: יונה, quoting זירא, says the תורבץ is only the bit of throat right next to the gullet.
steps.simpleTranslation: יונה said in the name of זירא: It is the throat area immediately bordering the gullet.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion on how to define the תורבץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a cutting test, this view defines the תורבץ by location: only the small strip of throat right where the gullet starts.

keyTerms.meaning: The swallowing area, the part of the throat right at the gullet

phrases.english: יונה said in the name of זירא:
the throat right at the gullet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the question of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורבץ is the throat area right next to the gullet.

steps.title: How big is the תורבץ? Between a wheat kernel and a barley kernel
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא gives the size: shorter than a barley kernel and longer than a wheat kernel.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much is it? רב אויא said: Less than a barley kernel and more than a wheat kernel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how large that strip is, and רב אויא gives a measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורבץ is a very small area, between the length of a wheat kernel and a barley kernel. So a cut only slightly higher or lower falls in a different zone.

phrases.english: And how much?
רב אויא said:
Less than a barley kernel
and more than a wheat kernel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a measurement to the definition in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The area is shorter than a barley kernel and longer than a wheat kernel.

steps.title: רבא declares the bull טריפה, using both רב's and שמואל's stringencies
steps.stepSummary: A bull's slaughter began in the תורבץ and was finished in the gullet. רבא applied the strict side of both רב and שמואל and ruled it טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a bull belonging to the sons of רב עוקבא. Its slaughter began in the entrance of the gullet and was finished in the gullet. רבא said: I place on it the stringencies of רב and the stringencies of שמואל, and I declare it טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: A real case where the רב/שמואל argument mattered in practice. רבא rules strictly by following both opinions where each is strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following שמואל, the תורבץ is not a place of slaughter, so the first cut there does not count as slaughter. Following רב, any hole in the תורבץ makes the animal טריפה. Put together, that first cut was a forbidden hole and not a valid slaughter, so the bull is טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Stringencies, the strict sides of a ruling

steps.whatToRemember: רבא ruled the bull טריפה by combining the strict side of רב with the strict side of שמואל. Step 30 shows that רבי אבא rejects this ruling, and step 31 brings a ברייתא against this kind of mixing.

phrases.english: A certain bull
that belonged to the sons of רב עוקבא,
where its slaughter began
in the entrance of the gullet,
and was finished in the gullet.
רבא said:
I impose on it the stringencies of רב
and the stringencies of שמואל,
and declare it טריפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא תּוֹרָא דַּהֲוָה לִבְנֵי רַב עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the argument of step 18 to a real case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא rules the bull טריפה by combining רב's and שמואל's stringencies. This ruling is later overturned by רבי אבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the passage: may a judge mix the strict side of one opinion with the strict side of another? רבי אבא (step 30) and the ברייתא (step 31) push back on this method.

steps.title: רבא explains his ruling with רב's strict view
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he used רב's strict rule: a hole of any size in the תורבץ makes the animal טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I used the strict side of רב, who said that a hole of any size makes it טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts explaining why he ruled the bull טריפה in step 24. He begins with the strict part he took from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cut began in the תורבץ. If that cut counts as a hole and not as slaughter, then רב's rule makes the animal טריפה, because for רב even a tiny hole there is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: By any amount, even a tiny bit
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after proper slaughter

phrases.english: [I applied] the stringencies of Rav,
phrases.notes: רבא is now explaining the ruling from the last step, where he called the bull טריפה.

phrases.english: for Rav said: [it is a tereifa if pierced] by any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבא's ruling in step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רב, a hole of any size in the תורבץ makes the animal טריפה.

steps.title: But רב holds the תורבץ is a valid place to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא raises an objection to himself: רב also says the תורבץ is a valid place to slaughter, so the cut there should count as kosher slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say it is a valid place for slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא voices the obvious objection to his own reasoning. He is setting up his next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you follow רב, the cut in the תורבץ is not a hole at all. It is the start of a kosher slaughter. So using רב to call it טריפה looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: A place on the neck where slaughter is valid
But didn't he say? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
It is a location [fit] for slaughter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 25 using another statement of the same רב
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of רב to declare the animal טריפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב treats the תורבץ as a place for slaughter, so for him the cut is kosher slaughter, not a disqualifying hole.

steps.title: On the location question, רבא follows שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that on this point he follows שמואל, who says the תורבץ is not a valid place to slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: I hold like שמואל, who says it is not a place for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the objection: on the location question he takes שמואל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל, the cut in the תורבץ is not slaughter, so it counts as a hole. Now רב's rule about a tiny hole can apply.

phrases.english: [I hold] like Shmuel, who says:
It is not a location [fit] for slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר: לָאו מְקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the issue: one question decided by שמואל, the other by רב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רב means following all of רב's views, including that the תורבץ is a place for slaughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא follows שמואל on location and רב on the size of the hole.

steps.title: But שמואל requires most of it to be pierced
steps.stepSummary: Second objection: שמואל says the animal is טריפה only if most of it was pierced, and this small cut was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you follow שמואל, doesn't he say it is טריפה only when most of it is pierced?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a second objection to himself. Now the problem is the size of the hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you follow שמואל on location, you should also follow him on the size of the hole. For שמואל, a small hole does not make the animal טריפה.

phrases.english: If [you follow] Shmuel, doesn't he say:
[Only if pierced] in its majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 27
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל also says only a majority hole makes it טריפה, so under שמואל this animal would be kosher.

steps.title: On the hole size, רבא follows רב
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that on the size of the hole he follows רב: any amount makes it טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I hold like רב, who says any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes his explanation. He takes רב's strict view on hole size together with שמואל's strict view on location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half of the ruling comes from a different sage, and in both cases it is the stricter half. That is what "the strict side of both רב and שמואל" means.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא combined two strict views: the תורבץ is not a place for slaughter (שמואל), and any hole there makes it טריפה (רב). In רבא's view, together they make the bull טריפה. The next step shows רבי אבא rejecting this.

phrases.english: [I hold] like Rav, who says: by any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 28 and completes רבא's reasoning
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the issue between two authorities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following שמואל means accepting his majority requirement.
steps.terutzMaskana: On hole size רבא follows רב, so even a small cut makes it טריפה.

steps.title: רבי אבא permits the bull and makes רבא pay
steps.stepSummary: The case reached רבי אבא, who said the bull is kosher under רב and under שמואל, and that רבא must pay the owner for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The story spread and reached רבי אבא. He told them: this bull is kosher, both according to רב and according to שמואל. Go tell the son of רב יוסף בר חמא to pay the owner the value of the bull.
steps.whatsHappening: Another sage, רבי אבא, overturns רבא's ruling. Because the bull was wrongly called טריפה, רבא has to pay for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא looks at each view as a whole. For רב, the תורבץ is a valid place to slaughter, so the cut is kosher. For שמואל, only a majority hole makes it טריפה, and this cut was not that. Neither sage on his own would forbid the bull.
steps.confusionAlert: "The son of רב יוסף בר חמא" is רבא himself. The bull's owner lost it because of רבא's ruling, so רבא is the one told to pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key question of the passage: may a judge combine the strict side of one opinion with the strict side of another, when neither opinion alone gives that result?

phrases.english: The matter circulated,
it came before Rabbi Abba,
he said to them: The bull,
both according to Rav and according to Shmuel, is permitted.
Go tell
the son of Rav Yosef bar Ḥama,
phrases.notes: This is רבא, the one who ruled the bull טריפה.

phrases.english: that he should pay the value of the bull to its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיגַּלְגַּל מִילְּתָא, מְטַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the ruling and reasoning of steps 24-29
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole practical ruling that the bull is טריפה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each sage's view must be taken as a whole, and under each view on its own the bull is permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא against mixing בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא brings a ברייתא: the halacha follows בית הלל, but a person may follow בית שמאי or בית הלל consistently. Whoever takes the leniencies of both is called wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר the son of רבינא said: I bring a refutation against "the enemies of רבא" (a polite way of meaning רבא himself). The הלכה always follows בית הלל. Someone who wants to act like בית שמאי may do so, and someone who wants to act like בית הלל may do so. But someone who takes the leniencies of בית שמאי and the leniencies of בית הלל is wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: A later sage brings a source to attack רבא's method of mixing two opinions. This source is only starting here and continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says you must follow one school consistently and may not pick and choose. This line condemns mixing leniencies. The part that hits רבא, who mixed stringencies, comes in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: "The enemies of רבא", a polite way of saying רבא himself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think מר בריה דרבינא is attacking רבא's enemies. Saying "enemies of" is just a polite way to avoid speaking harshly against רבא directly.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said:
I bring a refutation
against the enemies of Rava,
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying "against רבא".

phrases.english: The halakha is always according to the words of Beit Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי – עוֹשֶׂה,
phrases.english: but one who wishes to act according to the words of Beit Shammai may do so,
[and] according to the words of Beit Hillel may do so.

phrases.aramaic: מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית הִלֵּל – רָשָׁע.
phrases.english: [One who takes] the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the leniencies of Beit Hillel is wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא: מוֹתְבִינָא תְּיוּבְתָּא כְּלַפֵּי סָנְאֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבא's rejection by attacking רבא's method with a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's method of combining parts of רב's and שמואל's opinions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires following one opinion consistently and condemns picking and choosing between opposing schools.
